posts.title: Forum for posting comments on week 6 readings (due Oct 19)

items.name: 王玉美
items.note:
Monster are People too

This article discusses about an experiment that investigated the biases that mediates human gaze. I feel that the research activities done in this paper is interesting because they are doing the experiment and present the data in quantitative way. I have involved in several experiment activities and always has the thought that the lab study analysis is simpler and easily done by doing the qualitative approach. Like asking them about their experience during the study and so on. However, looking at this article, I feel that representing result in quantitative way may sometimes simpler and be able to extract more essences of result too. So, I think I should start to read more information about how we should present the data in quantitative way and looking more paper to get more examples about it.  This paper is indeed one of great and simple example to start with.

items.name: 李柏翰
items.note:
Animals behavior : Monsters are people too

In this article, Levy et al. discussed about the behavior of gaze following and what mediated the bias toward eyes. The conducted an experiment, which participants were presented with images of people, non-human creatures with eyes in the middle of their faces, or creature with eyes positioned elsewhere on their body.
This is an interesting experiment that tried to distinguished the hypothesis that configural face processing drives fixations to the middle of people's faces. The eyes fixation result showed that although the fixation models of humans and humanoids are different than the one of monsters, the subsequent fixations to the eyes are occurred rapidly, and concluding that human gaze selection is mediated by other brain mechanism, sensitive to eyes rather than only the head. The also gave implication for the studies of autism which didn't distinguish between gaze direction and head position, which make it unclear whether people with autism are lacking at targeting the head or eyes.

items.name: 張儷齡
items.note:
Animals behavior : Monsters are people too

This is a article about the target of our oculomotor system when we look at images of human, humanoids and monsters. research finding overturned the previous explanation, demonstrated the result is their eyes, not the middle of their head.

What I noticed after reading this article is his issue and application. It is not easy to find a question worthy of study, and there is a great model. I think this is a successful research, because of its result worth practicing in a wide scope, not only for individuals with autism but for character design and so on. And we could also found this valuable research topic would be solved just by a simple and violent way -- to record eye movements.

items.name: 劉  淨
items.note:
MacKenzie book. Chapter 5. Designing HCI Experiments

This article profoundly organize the essential concepts for experiment design while provides practical suggestions, considerable pitfalls and write-up tips.
It starts from the definition: experiment design is the process of deciding variables, tasks and procedure, how many participants and how to solicit them. Here, I list out some lessons from this article. (1) constrain number of independent under 3 to decrease interaction effects (2) consider data collection, organization and storage when we contrive a dependent variable, and the main reason we run pilot testing is to preliminary analyze on these consideration (3) choose a representative task that is similar to an actual usage, but be careful that an actual usage often includes secondary tasks that will harm internal validity (4) prevent learning effect especially for knowledge-based task (5) decide the number of participants by referring to similar research; insufficient amount of participants makes it hard to achieve statistical significance, while too many ones can bring statistical significance with not practical value.

items.name: 姚舜懷
items.note:
Monsters are People too


Levy et al. design an experiment according to their hypothesis: primates look at the eyes of creatures early, not just the centre of the face. In order to discuss the issue, they present the images with different types to the participants and their fixations are recorded. After the simple but precise experiment, they analyze the fixations data by repeated-measures ANOVA. They found that human gaze selection is sensitive to the eyes rather than face. We learned that how to deicide in/dependent variables, random variables ,and control variables through their experiment and also know that how to analyze data to get some findings.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
Animals Behavior: Monsters are people too

This essay says two explanations that mediates gaze following bias toward eyes and experiment with images of human, humanoid and monster. And these findings demonstrate that the eyes, and not the middle of the head, are being targeted by the oculomotor system. From experiment we can know that fixation to humans and humanoids went first to the centre of image and then shift vertically to their eyes; fixation on monster went to the centre of the image and then move in any possible direction as monster eyes were broadly distributed. Through the experiment of analysis and statistic data to gaze following, we can have an initial view toward how to do a quantitative research.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
Diehl & Stroebe (1987) - Productivity Loss in Brainstorming Groups: Toward the Solution of a Riddle

In this paper, only male participants were chosen to form brainstorming groups in Experiment 1 and 2. Apart from the lack of representative gender sampling, this practice was not mentioned throughout the discussions; perhaps the authors assumed that gender would not be relevant as a confounding variable in these brainstorming experiments. 

We had discussed in class about how we could try to determine which potential confounding variables are actually significant for the concerned experiment and how to possibly address issues caused by relevant confounding variables. However, there is a body of literature describing various sex differences in social behavior as well as varying effects caused by differential socialization between males and females. A 1976 study [1] comparing all-male, all-female, and mixed gender groups determined that there are many differences in communication style between all-male and all-female group dynamics that can be possible confounding factors in the context of group brainstorming. For example, in all-male groups males address significantly more interaction to the group as a whole (talking to the whole group vs. to an individual) than females in all-female groups - (36% and 30% vs 9% and 4%). 

[1] Aries, E. (1976). Interaction patterns and themes of male, female, and mixed groups. Small group behavior, 7(1), 7-18.

items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
Productivity Loss In Brainstorming Groups: Toward the Solution of a Riddle

    This paper research three factors which are considered main factors to contributing productivity loss in brainstorming groups. The three factors are evaluation apprehension, free riding, and blocking. The result shows that while evaluation apprehension dose significantly one’s production of ideas in individual brainstorming session, it does not have significant effect on brainstorming groups. Free ridding also be concluded not having significant effect on productivity loss in brainstorming loss.  Finally, they find blocking of  individual’s ideas due to waiting for others to express dose have an effect on productivity loss in brainstorming groups.

    I found it curious that the researcher of this paper explain the reason why free riding is not the issue here is because there is low costs of the individual contribution(e.g., effort, money,time), since the participants of brainstorming of groups are already committed to spending a set of period in the meeting place. That’s the typical case in the past, but now, since the online meeting and even mobile meeting is trending up, we cannot make sure everyone in the chatroom would commit to spending a set of period to fully engage in the brainstorming session, I wondered if free riding can be a issue when we bring brainstorming online.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
Data collection       

The article discuss several decisions need to be made of data collection, also including data pre-processing and data analysis. From removing noises in the dataset to operating in a system needs massive works in this process and how good the result depends on how people did in data collection.

The most impressive part to me is that observation provides an opportunity to pick up on nuances that may be lost in recording. When first stepping in no matter data mining or HCI field, I think observation just show the data distribution. However, it is not only that simple, we can find out more signal or information in the dataset. We can further implement clustering method to deeply dig in the data. That is why data mining is so popular nowadays.

items.name: 姚舜懷
items.note:
Designing HCI experiments

The chapter goes through the core details about how to design and conduct HCI experiments while explains what the experimental variables are. In the chapter, the author clearly takes a concrete example for demonstrating what confounding variables are and how confounding variables effect our analysis results. Moreover, the author also shows us many types of questionnaire designs and theirs suitable situations. I think the article is helpful for most beginners who are going to design and conduct an experiments with human participants.

items.name: 劉  淨
items.note:
How Did They Do That? The Ways and Means of Studying and Group Process

This paper gives a systematic view on understanding organizational behavior, while I think the method can also generalize to other qualitative studies. It talks about ways of data collection, constructing coding scheme, and analyzing data. It also discuss the trade-off between different ways. It makes me think about grounding theory that I would like to understand more it the two share similar concepts.

items.name: 劉  淨
items.note:
Productivity Loss In Brainstorming Groups: Toward the Solution of a Riddle

This research investigate three factors (free riding, evaluation apprehension, and production blocking) that typically considered to contribute to group productivity loss in group brain storming task. They conducted multiple experiments on each factors and compare their result to previous findings. 

First, in literature review, I found it fascinating that different research design different method on same problem. It is helpful to understand how researcher propose operational definition on single concept from different angle. The paper also presents a series of experiments that are coherent with one another, which is quite new for me (asking follow up question after a research).
